back: States have counted people and grain for thousands of years. A mean, median or mode turns a long table into one value you can compare.

title: Modal class on a histogram
back: The tallest bar is the modal class. The mode lies inside it, pulled towards the taller neighbour.

title: Mean: direct method
back: Use class marks $x_i$, the mid-points of the classes.

title: Mean: assumed mean
back: $a$ is a convenient class mark. Mind the minus signs.

title: Mean: step deviation
back: Do not forget the '× h' at the end.

title: Mode of grouped data
back: $f_1$ the modal class, $f_0$ the class before, $f_2$ the class after.

title: Median of grouped data
back: $cf$ is the cumulative frequency of the class before the median class.

title: Finding the median class
tex: \begin{gathered}\text{cf column}\\ \downarrow\\ \tfrac n2\\ \downarrow\\ \text{first cf}\ge\tfrac n2\\ \downarrow\\ l,\ cf,\ f,\ h\end{gathered}
back: The first class whose cf reaches n/2.

title: Empirical relationship
back: A rule of thumb: given two measures, estimate the third.

title: Which average?
tex: \begin{gathered}\text{mean: all values}\\ \text{median: the middle}\\ \text{mode: the peak}\end{gathered}
back: Extreme values pull the mean, hardly move the median, and do not touch the mode.
